edition: Issue #016 - A hung parliament dance card, gutsy All Whites, and one person's warehouse of buttons
tagline: Your 3-minute break. Zero fluff, maximum banter.

stories.headline: National crashes below 26%, Greens surge, and the Opportunity Party is everyone's awkward plus-one
stories.summary: A new RNZ-Reid Research poll has National at its lowest since 2020 on 25.9 percent, the Greens surging to 14.8 percent, and the 5.5 percent Opportunity Party projected as the tie-breaker neither coalition bloc can ignore.

body.text: A month out from voting day, the latest RNZ-Reid Research poll has shaken up the election picture. National has plunged 3.2 points to 25.9 percent, its weakest result since the 2020 election, while Labour also slipped 1.4 points to 30.8 percent, its third straight decline. The Greens made the biggest gain, jumping 4.6 points to 14.8 percent, their strongest showing this term. New Zealand First fell 1.3 points to 10.6 percent and ACT climbed 1.3 to 9 percent. On the numbers, neither the existing coalition nor a Labour-Greens-Te Pati Maori bloc would reach a 61-seat majority; the Opportunity Party's projected seven MPs would give either side the numbers to govern. Chris Hipkins leads Luxon 21.9 percent to 17.1 percent on preferred prime minister, and more than half of respondents (53.3 percent) rate Luxon's performance poorly.

Let's be honest about what this poll actually is: a nationwide maths problem where every party is insisting loudly that they are the only ones who know the answer, while one party that barely cleared the 5 percent fence sits there holding the keys. There is something beautifully silly about the idea that a government depends on a party polling 5.5 percent apologetically clearing its throat and saying, well, we hold the numbers now, so. Meanwhile Luxon collapsing to his worst rating while the country as a whole decides it is heading the wrong way is the political equivalent of finding out the whole dance floor thinks the music's bad but nobody has told the DJ. Vote, though. Seriously. That part is not a joke, and it does actually decide who holds the keys.

RNZ (6 Oct 2026, Craig McCulloch): RNZ-Reid Research poll of 1000 eligible voters online between 24 September and 1 October 2026 (quota-sampled, weighted by age/gender/geography, margin of error +/-3.1% at 95% confidence). Party vote: Labour 30.8%, National 25.9%, Greens 14.8%, NZ First 10.6%, ACT 9.0%, Opportunity 5.5%, Te Pati Maori 2.0%. National's 25.9% is its weakest since the 2020 election. Preferred PM: Hipkins 21.9%, Luxon 17.1% (Luxon down 2.8pts); 53.3% rate Luxon's performance poorly vs 29.6% well (net -23.7, his worst as leader). 53.1% say NZ is heading in the wrong direction. A 120-seat projection gives the current coalition 56 seats and Labour-Greens-Te Pati Maori 57; Opportunity's 7 MPs would lift either bloc to a majority (63 or 64).

stories.headline: All Whites frustrate Japan for an hour, take a Kirin Cup final to the wire, and still go home one goal short
stories.summary: The 86th-ranked All Whites pushed 17th-ranked Japan to a 2-1 loss in Tokyo's Kirin Cup final, levelling through Ben Old on the counter before a 71st-minute Ritsu Doan winner dashed hopes of a penalty shootout.

body.text: New Zealand went down 2-1 to Japan in the Kirin Cup final at Tokyo's Japan National Stadium on Monday night, but it was closer and scrappier than the scoreline suggests. Coach Darren Bazeley fielded an uncharacteristic back-five and defended deep in front of 67,000 mostly Japanese supporters against the 17th-ranked hosts. Ayase Ueda put Japan ahead in the 28th minute, but New Zealand levelled three minutes later when skipper Chris Wood dribbled clear on the break and laid off to Ben Old, who struck with his less-favoured right foot. Goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was exceptional, making nine saves. Ritsu Doan scored the 71st-minute winner, and Bazeley admitted it was disappointing not to force penalties. The 86th-ranked All Whites had earlier beaten China 3-0, drawn Palestine 2-2 and beaten Panama on penalties in the tournament. They next play India in Auckland (12 Nov) and Christchurch (15 Nov).

There is a special kind of sport heartbreak that comes from having done the hard bit perfectly and still losing, and the All Whites just bottled the whole thing in one frustrated 90 minutes. Love that we parked a bus in front of our own box, frustrated a side ranked 69 places above us in front of 67,000 of their own fans, kept it level deep into a cup final, and then the whole thing hinged on one 71st-minute moment. The fridge-magnet version of this game is we held Japan to a draw until 20 minutes from the end and only lost on a single goal, which is, you know, technically true and also the kind of silver lining you frame and hang somewhere you don't have to look at it every day. Sporting grief aside, genuinely proud of that effort. Nine saves from the keeper in a one-goal defeat is a beautiful, brutal stat.

RNZ Sport (6 Oct 2026): All Whites lost 2-1 to Japan in the Kirin Cup final at Japan National Stadium, Tokyo, in front of 67,000 supporters. Japan (FIFA rank 17) led through Ayase Ueda in the 28th minute; Ben Old levelled in the 31st after a counter-attack built by skipper Chris Wood (Old scored with his right foot). Goalkeeper Alex Paulsen made nine saves. Ritsu Doan scored the winner in the 71st minute. Coach Darren Bazeley fielded an unusual back-five. Earlier in the Asia window the All Whites drew Palestine 2-2, beat China 3-0, and beat Panama on penalties after 1-1. New Zealand are ranked 86th. Up next: two home matches against India, Auckland 12 Nov and Christchurch 15 Nov.

stories.headline: One woman, a closed-down haberdashery warehouse, and up to a million buttons: 'Bring your bags'
stories.summary: Auckland sustainability initiator Hannah Bennett ended up with hundreds of thousands of buttons a closing wholesaler gave her - she estimates 200,000 to 1.2 million - and is hosting a free ButtonFest this Friday: bring your bags and take as many as you can carry.

body.text: Auckland's Thread Lightly founder Hannah Bennett has found herself caretaker of what she estimates to be between 200,000 and 1.2 million buttons after a closing haberdashery wholesaler answered her call for help. She thought she was picking up a few boxes; it turned out to be an entire warehouse. So far 76 boxes are at her home - and that is only half of it. They are in the garage, the lounge, under the couch, with the kids stepping over them in the hallway. She has already shared bags with her local community and teachers, who use them in maths counting and art projects, but there are still far too many. This Friday afternoon she is holding ButtonFest at Highbury Community House in Birkenhead: free tables of buttons, bring your own bags, take as many as you can carry. The volunteer-run, free-to-access sustainability initiative has already rehomed an estimated 1.5 tonnes of fabric and craft supplies through its ThreadFest swaps.

We have all, at some point, said yes to one (1) small favour and watched it snowball into a full-time unpaid logistics job, but I suspect nobody has ever snowballed quite as magnificently as Hannah. One minute she is answering a call to help a haberdashery shut down, next minute the buttons are in the hallway, under the couch, and the kids are wading through them like a tiny, pastel snowdrift. The mental image of a grown adult standing at the door of a warehouse going oh no, that's the whole shop is genuinely the funniest thing in news this week. And instead of panicking she has done the most aggressively sensible and chaotic thing possible, which is hold a free event with a sign that says bring your bags and take as many as you can carry. Say what you like about Auckland; this is community spirit with buttons on. About a million of them.

RNZ Nights (5 Oct 2026): Hannah Bennett, founder of the volunteer-run sustainability initiative Thread Lightly (launched April last year after she noticed a lack of fabric swaps in Auckland), received hundreds of thousands of buttons from a closing haberdashery wholesaler. She estimates the collection at 200,000 to 1.2 million; 76 boxes are currently at her home, about half the total. She has already shared buttons with local community and teachers for maths counting exercises and art projects. ButtonFest is this Friday afternoon at Highbury Community House, Birkenhead, Auckland - free, bring your own bags. Thread Lightly's ThreadFest swaps have rehomed an estimated 1.5 tonnes of fabric and craft supplies; the next ThreadFest is 31 October at Birkdale Community House.

affiliate_cta.headline: Got a hobby itch, or a lot of tiny things to wrangle?
affiliate_cta.body: Between a warehouse-load of buttons and a national mood change, this week is a decent moment to start or refresh a small creative project of your own. A couple of harmless starting points for the crafter, the collector, or anyone who has ever looked at a drawer on the verge of winning. No pressure, no commitment.
